Verbs Used to Express Decision Making

Business negotiations can be time consuming and you may run the risk of not getting what you wanted in the first place. Therefore, expressing yourself clearly and confidently will ensure you got your message across the way you intended.

Here are some verbs you can use to express yourself clearly in a negotiation.

• agreed - use this verb to show that you decided together what will be done and how it will be done

    • We agreed on a price including the website.

    • This is the domain we agreed on.

    • As we agreed, we'll be responsible for updates on the company's activities.

    • We agreed to the purchase of a new domain.

  • suggest - use this verb to tell the other party about something that may be useful or suitable for a particular purpose

    • I would suggest making the payment upfront.

    • I strongly / seriously / tactfully suggest training the staff immediately.

    • I suggest calling her before we proceed.

  • settle (on) - use this verb to make a decision between two or more people

    • We have finally settled on a final price of 8 million dollars.

    • We have settled on delivering the training.

    • I settled on a name for the website.

  • want - use this verb to express what you would like to do

    • I want to let her that we have settled on a price.

    • I want to agree on a final price.

  • take care - use this phrasal verb to express what is necessary to do to deal with a person or situation

    • We shall take care of the staff training.

    • The staff training has been taken care of.

    • Janet will take care of the final arrangements.
Closing the Deal in a Negotiation

In a business negotiation, it is important to know when and how to complete a transaction or negotiation. You need to make sure the other party understands your terms and any other actions that need to be taken.

Here is some language you can use to ensure you can close a deal.

1. Start with a summary
    Let's summarize what we've decided.
    At this point, I could summarize what we've agreed on.
  2. State and confirm the terms of the agreement
    We've agreed to ... the purchase of the company / buy a new website domain.
    We've settled on ... a final price / new name for the website.
    As agreed, we'll take care of ... training the new staff / the final arrangements.
  3. Ask for confirmation on missing details
    Are there any details that still need to be taken care of?
    Are there any details that still need to be worked out?
  4. Further actions to be taken
    We'll need you to ... supply us with information regarding the training / arrange a follow up meeting
    The question of ... cost / prices ... remains to be clarified.
  5. Sealing the deal
    Shall we ... move to the pen and paper / seal the deal?

Farmani: Alright Miranda, let's summarize what we've agreed on.
Miranda: Absolutely. We've agreed to the purchase of the domain www.wearholly's.com and settled on a final price of eight million dollars for the domain name and our PR services which include blogging, online articles, callouts, events, a Business Link page and updates on the company's events.
Farmani: Good job. Shall we go ahead with the purchase of our inventory tracking system?

Miranda: Yes. I talked to the company who created the system and we've settled on paying $30,000 which can be payable upfront or in 12 monthly installments.
Farmani: Which is your preference?
Miranda: Since we are yet unfamiliar with the system, I would strongly suggest paying in installments. We can always return it if we're dissatisfied.
Farmani: Are there any details that still need to be taken care of?
Miranda: As agreed, we'll take care of training the staff for online sales. However, we'll need you to supply us with information about your training needs.

Farmani: Let's save that for another meeting. I'll need to review our discussion with personnel first. Shall we move to the pen and paper?
Miranda: May I send a quick call to Janet first? I want to let her know that we've proceeded to this point.
Farmani: Absolutely. Let me show you an office where you'll have some privacy.
